title: AI-Optimized Smart Grids: Powering India's Renewable Energy Transition for a Sustainable Digital Economy
summary: Abstract India's transition toward a renewable energy-led economy faces critical challenges in grid stability, demand forecasting, and efficient integration of intermittent power sources such as solar and wind. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly central to overcoming these constraints, enabling predictive load forecasting, real-time fault detection, and autonomous demand-response management across smart grid. Grid Mission, the IndiaAI Mission, and NITI Aayog's National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence. It further examines barriers to scale, including high implementation costs, inconsistent data interoperability across state utilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities in AI-integrated grid systems, and the skills gap in AI-energy hybrid expertise. Through a review-based analytical framework, the paper proposes an integrated model aligning AI-enabled smart grid deployment with SDG-7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG-13 (Climate Action) within India's Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The findings suggest that AI-optimized energy systems, if scaled with supportive policy and skilled workforce development, can position India as a global leader in sustainable, technology-driven energy infrastructure.

title: INNOVATION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: INVESTIGATING THE BIDIRECTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TECHNOLOGICAL INNOVATION AND DIGITAL SERVICES TRADE
summary: This study examines the bidirectional relationship between digital services trade and technological innovation, as well as the distinct dynamics of the relationship between exports and imports. Using a three-stage least squares estimation approach on panel data from 83 economies from 2014 to 2021, findings reveal a positive and statistically significant two-way relationship between digital services trade and innovation output. Exports and imports of digital services are positively associated with technological innovation, and innovation corresponds positively to the digital services trade. While innovation exerts a substantial and elastic relationship with digital trade, the association between trade and innovation is modest and inelastic. Moreover, innovation has a stronger relationship with digital services exports than with imports, while imports exert a more pronounced link with innovation than exports. The findings imply policy priorities on financial access support, institutional quality, human capital, digital infrastructure and balanced regulations to foster innovation and digital services trade.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis: Cradle-to-gate supply chain emissions and scale-dependent cost analysis
summary: This study presents an integrated assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis that combines experimentally validated lifecycle inventory data, comprehensive cradle-to-gate greenhouse gas accounting, and probabilistic techno-economic analysis under scale-dependent conditions. The results demonstrate that under a realistic Net Zero 2050 grid scenario, the total carbon footprint is estimated at 2.53 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , with electricity consumption dominating the environmental impact. However, evaluating the system under an ideal zero‑carbon electricity supply reveals a baseline footprint of 0.44 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , demonstrating that upstream material production and component manufacturing impose an irreducible minimum emission threshold. Economically, the levelized cost of hydrogen decreases from $8.16/kgH 2 at a production scale of 1,000 kgH 2 /day to $5.05/kgH 2 at 50,000 kgH 2 /day, driven primarily by economies of scale. Notably, the two-parameter interaction analysis reveals that system availability and electrochemical efficiency act as primary co-optimization drivers, exhibiting a pronounced synergistic interaction for global warming potential while delivering additive economic benefits for hydrogen production cost. Furthermore, increasing system scale not only lowers costs but also progressively narrows economic uncertainty. These findings highlight that the sustainability of green hydrogen cannot be accurately evaluated without incorporating upstream supply chain impacts alongside operational metrics. The study provides an evidence-based framework for evaluating emerging electrolysis technologies and informing rigorous carbon certification standards.

title: Aligning Financial Education with the National Education Policy: Towards a Strategic Framework for Developing Informed Capital Market Investors
summary: Indian Capital Markets have demonstrated strong performance and have been instrumental in economic prosperity over the years. They are not only helping the capital formation but also a source of employment generation and wealth creation. There are a lot of investors into the market who wish to earn quick money but they do not have proper knowledge and training. As a result they suffer losses and create panic into the market. Finally, a message spreads among investors and general public that investing into the capital market is very risky and they avoid this prominent investment avenue. Most of these participants are youth. On the other hand a very small portion of Indian population is financially literate. This paper helps in resolving these two major issues i.e. to make sure the presence of financially educated investors into the Capital market and to make sure that the common people of country become financially literate. The present study suggests that the new National Education Policy will be proved as a very effective tool to achieve both of these two goals without the involvement of huge resources. With the help of Logic Model this study proposes the creation of a framework through which the young generation of country will be properly informed and trained about the structure, the risk and the rewards associated with the capital markets. So they may envision it as a career opportunity or they may be very well informed investors. Similarly, through the Credit - based Projects in their undergraduate / postgraduate programmes, these students will help in increasing the financial literacy of the common citizens of the country.

title: Digital Transformation of Municipal Corporations in India: Opportunities and Challenges for Achieving the Viksit Bharat 2047 Vision
summary: Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 seeks to transform the country into a developed nation by the centenary of independence. Municipal corporations have a central role in this transformation because the quality of urban governance directly affects citizens’ everyday lives, economic activity, environmental sustainability and social well-being. Rapid urbanisation, increasing demand for public services, climate-related risks and growing expectations for transparent administration have created a need for municipal institutions to adopt digital technologies. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital transformation of municipal corporations in India. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, cloud computing, digital payment systems, data analytics, Internet of Things applications and online citizen-service platforms can improve municipal administration. Particular attention is given to digital revenue collection, solid-waste management, water and sanitation services, urban planning, grievance redressal, traffic management and citizen participation. The paper argues that digital transformation should not be understood merely as the computerisation of existing municipal processes. Instead, it should involve institutional reform, data-driven decision-making, inclusive service delivery, employee capacity building, cybersecurity and sustainable urban development. At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

title: Does Economic Policy Uncertainty Influence ESG Performance? Evidence from European Banking Sector
summary: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the impact of economic policy uncertainty (EPU) on environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance in the European banking sector and then to investigate the moderating influence of board gender diversity (BGD) on this relationship. We analyzed a sample of 113 European Union banks for the period 2016-2024 and we developed an econometric model applying a dynamic panel data regression analysis (generalized Method of Moments – GMM System) on 1,017 bank-year observations. To test research hypotheses, we considered BGD in terms of female participation on the board of directors and we measured ESG dimensions by using the ESG score provided by LSEG Refinitiv. The results highlight that EPU affects the ESG performance of European banks and specifically, demonstrate that EPU reduces the overall ESG score. EPU also declines governance and environmental engagements but enhances the social activities to dampen uncertainty during periods of high EPU. This study also suggests that the presence of women on board mitigate these negative effects since the influence of EPU on overall ESG performance is positive in this circumstance. The investigation is highly relevant for regulators, policymakers, potential investors, managers and other stakeholders who are interested in improving the ESG performance of banks under different uncertainties. In this regard, the study represents a significant avenue for future research, with relevant implications for both theory and practice. Our study significantly contributes to the existing literature on the relationship between EPU and ESG in developed countries such as the European context. In this regard, our research is the first that offers insights about the influence of the EPU on ESG performance in the European banking sector.

title: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Development in the Niger Delta: Community Participation, Environmental Governance, and the Road to Achieving the SDGs 2030
summary: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria represents one of the most ecologically significant yet environmentally vulnerable ecosystems globally. Since the onset of oil and gas exploration in the 1950s, the region has experienced severe environmental degradation manifested through oil spills, gas flaring, deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and declining fish populations. These anthropogenic activities have led to biodiversity loss, compromised ecosystem services, and heightened socio-economic vulnerabilities among local communities. This study critically examines the intersection between biodiversity conservation and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030, with emphasis on aligning local actions with global development frameworks. Using a multidisciplinary approach, the study synthesizes findings from existing literature, policy reviews, and community-based interventions to explore the roles of biodiversity in achieving key SDGs such as poverty alleviation (Goal 1), food security (Goal 2), clean water (Goal 6), climate action (Goal 13), and ecosystem protection (Goals 14 and 15). The analysis reveals that current efforts to conserve biodiversity in the Niger Delta are fragmented, inadequately enforced, and hindered by weak governance structures and limited community engagement. The paper recommends a holistic strategy that integrates strengthened environmental legislation, green technology adoption, participatory governance, and ecosystem restoration programs. The findings underscore that biodiversity protection is not merely an environmental obligation but a prerequisite for economic stability, public health, and sustainable livelihoods. Achieving SDGs 2030 in the Niger Delta will require coordinated action among government agencies, industry stakeholders, NGOs, and local communities to reverse ecosystem degradation and secure a resilient future.

title: The Role of Ownership Structure and Real Earnings Management on the Firm Performance of Non-Financial Firms Listed in Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study investigates the impact of real earnings management (REM) on firm performance and the moderating role of ownership structure among non-financial firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Grounded in agency and stakeholder theories, the research examines how different forms of ownership specifically managerial and institutional shape the relationship between REM and firm profitability, measured through Return on Assets (ROA). Using panel data from 2008 to 2023, the study employs a dynamic panel regression model to control for firm-specific effects and potential endogeneity. The findings reveal that REM positively influences short-term profitability, but its effect is significantly moderated by ownership structure. Managerial ownership enhances overall firm performance but intensifies the negative impact of REM on ROA, suggesting potential overuse or ineffective application of REM strategies when managers hold significant equity stakes. Conversely, institutional ownership not only directly improves profitability but also weakens the positive impact of REM, reflecting its governance role in constraining opportunistic managerial behavior. These results highlight the dual influence of ownership structure in both enhancing firm performance and regulating earnings management practices. The study offers valuable insights for corporate managers, investors, and policymakers on the importance of tailoring governance mechanisms to mitigate REM risks and ensure sustainable financial performance.

title: Blockchain Enabled Circular Supply Chain Management for Product Lifecycle Tracking and Consumer Incentives: A Case Study in Sri Lanka
summary: Closing the post-consumer loop remains a persistent challenge in waste management and pollution control. While blockchain technology has improved upstream traceability, most systems terminate tracking at the point of sale, leaving consumer disposal undocumented. This blind spot undermines circular economy implementation, limits Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance, and exacerbates municipal solid waste pollution. This study addresses this gap by developing a blockchain-enabled tracking framework that integrates an immutable ledger for life cycle tracking, a consumer mobile application for disposal registration, and IoT-enabled smart disposal machines to verify physical waste recovery events. The system’s technical feasibility was validated through a functional prototype and Minimum Viable Product (MVP) blockchain validation, confirming efficient transaction handling and secure life cycle updates. Furthermore, socio-technical factors driving user adoption of this green technology were evaluated using an empirical survey (*r* = .72, *p* < .001) and stakeholder interviews. This research provides an enhanced framework incorporating Digital Product Passports (DPP) to improve global material recovery and reduce environmental contamination. The system architecture is evaluated across high-impact waste streams including fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), automotive parts, and electronic waste (mobile phones) while contextualizing regional regulatory challenges against global sustainability standards. Visual diagrams and policy comparison analyses support a clearer understanding of life cycle traceability and tech-driven pollution mitigation. These contributions offer a validated, scalable framework that organizations can leverage to enhance consumer participation, improve material recovery, and enable data-driven environmental management.

title: Transition Design for a Sustainable Meat and Alternatives Supply Chain in Japan: Three Transition Scenarios Envisioning Future Food Systems
summary: This study explores the transition toward a sustainable meat and alternative protein supply chain in Japan using a transition design approach. Amid growing global demands for sustainability in livestock systems, Japan faces unique challenges, such as geographical and structural constraints and low consumer awareness regarding sustainability and animal welfare. The aim of this study is to address the structural issues within Japan’s protein supply system and present sustainable transition scenarios. Through detailed interviews with 21 frontrunners and co-creation workshops, the structural challenges of the current socio-technical regime that hinder transition were analyzed, and a theory of change was developed. The findings reveal that Japan’s meat and protein supply systems are locked into unsustainable practices due to regulatory, cognitive, and normative rules. Based on these insights, three transition scenarios are proposed: “Grazed Lean Beef as a Feast,” “Localized Circular Communities,” and “Food Printer”. These scenarios emphasize the importance of experimental networks, culturally grounded visions, and phased interventions. This study contributes to the theoretical understanding of sustainable transitions in the food sector and provides practical strategies for policymakers and industry stakeholders in Japan.

title: AI-driven business analytics for sustainable supply chain management in African agribusiness: a PLS-SEM and machine learning approach
summary: Purpose This study examines the associations between artificial intelligence capabilities, supply chain performance, and sustainability outcomes in African agribusiness. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, it investigates the direct relationships between AI capabilities and sustainability outcomes, as well as the mediating role of supply chain performance in translating AI capabilities into environmental and resource efficiency gains. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from executives and managers across large-scale farms and agricultural multinationals operating in six African countries. The conceptual model and hypotheses were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling and machine learning algorithms. Findings AI capabilities are positively associated with supply chain performance, which in turn corresponds with improved environmental impact, resource efficiency, sustainability reporting, overall sustainability, and general AI perception. Mediation analysis suggests that supply chain performance serves as a transmission mechanism linking AI capabilities to sustainability outcomes. Machine learning models achieved strong predictive accuracy across most sustainability dimensions. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal inference. The sample is drawn from six African countries, which may restrict generalizability. Future research should employ longitudinal designs and expand to other emerging economies. Originality/value This study extends the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory to AI-enabled sustainable supply chain management in African agribusiness, an empirically under-researched context. It delineates both direct and indirect pathways through which AI capabilities relate to sustainability outcomes and introduces a dual-analytical approach combining PLS-SEM and machine learning for explanatory and predictive insights.

title: Winning Consumer Trust Through Supply Chain Responsibility Communication: How Certification, Disclosure, and Beneficiary Framing Shape Credibility
summary: ABSTRACT As stakeholders increasingly demand supply chain transparency, companies face a legitimacy paradox: disclosing supply chain responsibility (SR) information is necessary to meet stakeholder expectations, yet disclosure can invite scrutiny rather than build credibility. Drawing on and extending legitimacy theory, this study investigates which attributes of SR communication resolve this paradox by enhancing credibility among consumers. Three vignette‐based experimental studies manipulate key attributes: disclosure presence, certification source, disclosure basis, metric focus, and beneficiary emphasis. Results show that SR communication significantly enhances perceived credibility compared to no communication, with social responsibility generating stronger effects than environmental responsibility—an asymmetry that disappears once communication is framed around worker rather than firm benefits. Third‐party certification substantially increases credibility compared to self‐certification, but this advantage diminishes when companies report relevant, verifiable outcomes, revealing that structural and consequential forms of legitimacy can substitute for one another. Contrary to expectations, voluntary disclosure does not enhance credibility over mandatory disclosure. Most notably, emphasizing benefits for supply chain workers generates significantly higher credibility than emphasizing benefits for the buying company, demonstrating the moral power of other‐oriented communication. The study extends legitimacy theory to consumer evaluations of supply chain practices, showing how companies can resolve the legitimacy paradox through specific communication design choices, and offers actionable guidance: companies should prioritize third‐party certification when outcome evidence is unavailable, and emphasize worker welfare over operational benefits.

title: China's dual-carbon narrative and bio-based flame-retardant supply chains: Industrial economics of phosphorylated recycled cellulose
summary: This study examines the industrial economics of phosphorylated recycled cellulose flame retardants (PR-CFR) within China's dual-carbon policy framework, targeting peak carbon emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Using a provincial panel dataset covering 28 Chinese provinces over 2008–2023, the study employs a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM), dynamic panel GMM, double-threshold panel regression, and mediation analysis to investigate how phosphorylation technology intensity, green procurement policy, and recycled cellulose feedstock availability jointly drive bio-based flame-retardant (bio-FR) industry total factor productivity (TFP), carbon footprint reduction, and downstream value chain integration. The principal results are fourfold. First, phosphorylation technology intensity exerts a direct effect of 0.312 and a spatial spillover effect of 0.168 on bio-FR industry TFP, confirming significant cross-provincial technology diffusion in the green chemical materials sector. Second, a double-threshold nonlinearity exists in the relationship between phosphorylation intensity and TFP: regime-specific coefficients are 0.102, 0.248, and 0.386 below, between, and above estimated thresholds of 0.35 and 0.70 on a normalized intensity scale, indicating that technology concentration above the upper threshold generates superadditive productivity returns. Third, carbon intensity reduction mediates 30.6 % of the total effect of the dual-carbon policy synergy index on bio-FR industry eco-efficiency, identifying decarbonization as the primary channel through which policy instruments translate into industrial competitiveness. Fourth, the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index for bio-based FR production has declined from 0.482 in 2008–0.171 in 2023, signaling a structural transition from monopolistic concentration toward competitive market organization as entry barriers fall with maturing phosphorylation technology. The findings advance the industrial economics of sustainable chemistry and offer policy guidance for accelerating China's bio-based flame retardant supply chain transition.

title: Digital Transformation, Green Logistics Capability, and Operational Efficiency in Indonesian Freight Forwarding: The Sequential Mediating Mechanisms of Technology Adoption and Service Excellence
summary: This study examines the sequential mediating roles of technology adoption and service excellence in the relationships among digital transformation, green logistics capability, and operational efficiency in Indonesian freight forwarding companies. This quantitative causal-explanatory research employed a cross-sectional survey of 250 managers from freight forwarding companies in Indonesia. Data analysis utilized Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 and bootstrapping with 5,000 subsamples. Data analysis utilized Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 3.0 and bootstrapping with 5,000 subsamples. The findings confirm all seven direct hypotheses and both sequential mediation hypotheses. Digital transformation significantly influences technology adoption (β=0.385, p<0.001), while green logistics capability positively affects technology adoption (β=0.342, p<0.001). Technology adoption substantially enhances service excellence (β=0.431, p<0.001), which in turn drives operational efficiency (β=0.402, p<0.001). Crucially, the sequential mediation pathways—digital transformation → technology adoption → service excellence → operational efficiency and green logistics capability → technology adoption → service excellence → operational efficiency—are both significant, demonstrating that technology adoption and service excellence function as complementary sequential mechanisms. This research provides theoretical contributions by extending dynamic capabilities theory through the identification of sequential micro-foundations and offers practical implications for forwarding managers, industry associations, and policymakers regarding integrated digital and green strategies.

title: Carbon Cost Information Collection and Consolidation from an ESG Perspective: A Case Study of Kingfa
summary: Purpose: To examine how carbon cost information is collected and consolidated from an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) perspective, using Kingfa Science & Technology as a case study. Specifically, the study aims to address the fragmentation of carbon-related physical and financial data across corporate systems and to construct a practical framework for carbon cost classification, attribution, and consolidation, thereby supporting the "dual-carbon" goals and responding to external pressures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Methodology: This study adopts a single-case study approach based on publicly available secondary data, including Kingfa's annual reports (2022–2025), sustainability reports (2022–2025), and the China Carbon Market Development Report (2025). Data analysis employs trend comparison to track the co-movement of green business expansion and carbon intensity changes, and monetary conversion estimation using market reference prices to bridge physical energy consumption data with financial cost information. The analysis covers Scope 1 (direct emissions) and Scope 2 (energy indirect emissions), with Scope 3 addressed qualitatively by materiality, since public reporting provides it only as an unverified group-level aggregate that cannot be attributed to a cost object. Findings: The study reveals that Kingfa's carbon cost information is highly fragmented across ESG, energy, production, R&D, and financial systems, with no effective mapping between physical emission data and financial cost data. Three major gaps are identified: (1) inconsistent classification and accounting boundaries of carbon costs; (2) lack of mapping between physical and monetary data; and (3) unclear cost objects and cost drivers. To address these gaps, the study proposes a carbon cost collection and consolidation mechanism comprising: (a) a three-tier classification framework dividing carbon costs into carbon emission costs, carbon abatement costs, and carbon risk costs; (b) a tripartite "cost object–cost driver–responsibility center" consolidation structure that clarifies cost attribution, allocation basis, and accountable entities. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The proposed mechanism enhances the traceability and managerial relevance of carbon cost information, filling the research gap on front-end information collection and consolidation from an ESG perspective. For practice, it provides Kingfa and similar manufacturing enterprises with a structured approach to integrating fragmented carbon data into managerial decision-making. For policy, the study offers empirical insights for regulators and standard-setters to consider enterprise-level carbon cost accounting frameworks that align with both domestic "dual-carbon" targets and international mechanisms such as CBAM.

title: A Study of Institutional Governance and Digital Transformation of the Varkari Kirtan Tradition in Maharashtra: Emerging Opportunities and Administrative Challenges.
summary: Abstract The Varkari Kirtan tradition represents an important component of Maharashtra’s cultural and spiritual heritage and has historically contributed to social awareness, community participation and the transmission of values across generations. However, rapid technological development and changing patterns of communication have created new possibilities as well as challenges for the preservation and promotion of this traditional practice. The present study examines the role of institutional governance in facilitating the digital transformation of the Varkari Kirtan tradition in Maharashtra. It focuses on the emerging use of digital platforms for documentation, dissemination, accessibility, cultural promotion and livelihood opportunities. The study also examines the administrative challenges associated with digitalization, including systematic documentation, institutional coordination, digital accessibility, authenticity, commercialization and the need for sustainable policy interventions. The study is descriptive and exploratory in nature and is primarily based on secondary data collected from research literature, books, government publications, institutional sources and credible digital resources. The study highlights that digital transformation can strengthen the visibility, accessibility and preservation of Varkari Kirtan, provided that appropriate institutional mechanisms and administrative support are established. The paper suggests greater institutional collaboration, digital documentation, capacity building and policy support for ensuring the sustainable preservation and development of the Varkari Kirtan tradition in the contemporary digital era.

title: AI-ENABLED DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE IN SMES: A STRATEGIC ANALYSIS WITHIN THE SPANISH BUSINESS ECOSYSTEM
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency, strengthen innovation capabilities, and sustain long-term competitiveness. Within the Spanish business ecosystem, digital transformation has accelerated over the past decade due to technological progress, evolving customer expectations, and supportive national and European digitalization policies. Nevertheless, the adoption of AI among Spanish SMEs remains uneven, with significant differences across sectors, organizational capabilities, and regional innovation environments. This study examines how AI-driven digital transformation contributes to competitive advantage in Spanish SMEs from a strategic management perspective. Rather than treating AI as a standalone technological solution, the paper considers it an organizational capability that reshapes decision-making, resource allocation, customer engagement, and business model innovation. The discussion integrates perspectives from the resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, digital transformation research, and innovation management to explain the strategic mechanisms through which AI creates sustainable value. Particular attention is given to organizational readiness, leadership, digital culture, workforce skills, data governance, and ecosystem collaboration. The study also evaluates the challenges that continue to limit AI implementation, including financial constraints, technological complexity, cybersecurity concerns, regulatory compliance, and shortages of digital talent. The findings suggest that sustainable competitive advantage depends not solely on technological investment but on the ability of SMEs to integrate AI into strategic planning, organizational learning, and continuous innovation processes. The Spanish experience demonstrates that successful AI adoption emerges from the interaction between internal capabilities and external institutional support, providing valuable insights for SMEs operating in similar economic environments.

title: Determinants of Digital Marketing Adoption and MSME Performance in Indonesia’s Halal Food Sector
summary: Background Digital transformation has become a strategic pillar of Indonesia’s economy, with an estimated contribution of USD 130 billion by 2025. Halal Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in the food and beverage sector, contribute approximately USD 180 billion annually, account for around 60% of Indonesia’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and employ nearly 97% of the national workforce. However, digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs remains limited due to low digital literacy, inadequate infrastructure, financial constraints, and inconsistent implementation of sharia business principles. This study examines the determinants of digital marketing adoption and its influence on the performance of halal MSMEs in Indonesia. Methods This study employed an explanatory quantitative research design based on the Technology–Organization–Environment–Personal (TOEP) framework. Data were collected from 500 halal-certified MSMEs operating in the food and beverage sector across Indonesia using a structured questionnaire. Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 was used to evaluate the relationships among technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors, digital marketing adoption, and business performance. Results The findings indicate that technological, organizational, environmental, and personal factors significantly influence digital marketing adoption among halal MSMEs. Furthermore, digital marketing adoption has a positive and significant effect on business performance by improving operational efficiency, increasing customer loyalty, strengthening halal brand visibility, and enhancing overall business competitiveness. Conclusions Digital marketing adoption is a key strategic driver for improving the competitiveness and sustainability of halal MSMEs in Indonesia. Strengthening digital capabilities through technological readiness, organizational support, favorable business environments, and personal competencies is essential to accelerate digital transformation and maximize the contribution of halal MSMEs to the national digital economy.

title: AI and Digital Transformation in Smart Tourism: A Bibliometric Mapping of Emerging Labor, Skills, and Educational Research Directions
summary: Smart tourism research has grown rapidly alongside the post-pandemic acceleration of digital-technology adoption, yet much of this literature foregrounds business and operational outcomes while leaving the social and educational consequences of AI-driven transformation comparatively underexamined. This paper maps the intellectual structure of smart-tourism scholarship at the intersection of digital transformation and organizational dynamic capability, with particular attention to the labor, skills, and educational dimensions of this shift. A bibliometric search of 468 Scopusindexed publications (2020-2025) was analyzed using VOSviewer (version 1.6) to produce overlay, network, and density visualizations of keyword cooccurrence and thematic evolution. The results show that while the dominant intellectual core of the field remains digital transformation and dynamic capability, a growing secondary cluster addresses workforce readiness, digital literacy, and small-enterprise adaptation - themes with direct bearing on labor markets and vocational education. The temporal mapping indicates that research has moved from conceptual technology-adoption frameworks (2020-2022) toward applied studies of organizational and workforce change (2023-2025). Malaysia's tourism sector is examined here as an illustrative case of a digitally maturing economy, offering a lens on how infrastructure investment under Sustainable Development Goal 9 intersects with skills and educational policy. The paper argues that the literature's continuing emphasis on efficiency outcomes leaves its social and educational questions who is retrained, who is displaced, and how tourism-education systems should respond - comparatively underdeveloped, and it proposes a research and policy agenda oriented toward these questions.

title: From Conduit to Compliance Node: The Institutional Evolution of Supply Chain Intermediary Liability in China’s Anti-Counterfeiting Regime, 1979–2026
summary: Background: Counterfeit goods realize illicit value only when moved, mainly by logistics intermediaries rather than counterfeiters, so how the law treats these intermediaries determines where enforcement can bite. This review traces the policies, laws, literature, and data relevant to China’s anti-counterfeiting landscape from 1979 to 2026. Methods: A narrative review combined a PRISMA 2020-guided search of Scopus and Web of Science (108 peer-reviewed publications) with 14 primary legal instruments and 4 types of institutional grey literature. Institutional theory was used to derive four expectations. Results: Four regulatory phases were identified, across which duties migrated toward logistics chokepoints: criminal accomplice liability (2004), civil facilitation liability, customs detention, platform liability, parcel-level identity, inspection and screening duties, franchisor network supervision (2024), and independent liability for assisting confusion (2025). Expectations of external origin, chokepoint migration, and ceremonial compliance were supported; capacity-calibrated decoupling awaits verification. Obligations were synthesized into an actor-by-actor matrix. Official data show that only about 3% of administrative cases reach criminal referral, with no breakdown by intermediary type. Conclusions: China has converted logistics intermediaries from neutral conduits into liability-bearing compliance nodes under a know-your-consignor regime calibrated to large integrated operators, but this regime still relies primarily on coercive measures.

title: Digital Media Consumption in India’s Digital Economy: Associations Between Parenting Styles and Social Media Mediation Strategies
summary: The world is witnessing an unprecedented surge in children’s exposure to digital technologies across socioeconomic segments. This shift presents both opportunities and challenges for parents, who must navigate the complex interplay between traditional parenting norms and the demands of digital mediation. This study examines the association between general parenting styles and the adoption of digital mediation strategies. Using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were gathered from three hundred and seven parents in four major Indian cities. Using validated scales, correspondence analysis was performed to examine the relationship between parenting styles and mediation strategies. The findings indicate a significant association between general parenting styles and predominant digital mediation strategies. Authoritative parenting was most frequently associated with authoritarian surveillance in the present sample, whereas authoritarian parenting was primarily associated with restrictive mediation and non-intrusive inspection. No respondent was classified as predominantly permissive under the adopted classification procedure. The aggregate level of social media mediation did not differ significantly across education, household income, number of children, or caregiver-related characteristics. The findings provide insights into the evolving landscape of digital parenting in India and highlight the potential value of initiatives that support parents in navigating children’s digital engagement. It bridges a vital research gap by situating digital parenting within India’s sociocultural environment and contributes to the broader theoretical discourse on digital parenting.

title: Mapping the gender attrition gap in academic psychology.
summary: Women comprise the majority of students and early-career scholars in psychology, yet they are less likely to remain active in research over time. This pattern raises a central question: At what stages of academic careers do women disproportionately leave academia, and what factors drive their attrition? Using large-scale bibliometric data tracking 78,216 psychologists who began publishing between 2000 and 2014, we examine gender differences in research career attrition operationalized through publishing activity across the full trajectory from entry onward. Although women accounted for more than 60\% of new entrants, they experienced higher attrition rates than men, with the gender gap peaking approximately five years after first publication. Early-career performance, particularly first-authored publications, was the strongest predictor of subsequent retention, whereas last-authored publications were most closely associated with continued activity at later career stages. Collaboration patterns and institutional context also shaped career persistence, though less strongly than publication indicators. Notably, gender differences in research attrition persisted even after accounting for these career determinants, especially during early career stages. These findings suggest that gender inequality in psychology is driven less by recruitment than by differential retention over time. Addressing early-career vulnerability may therefore be essential to achieving equitable representation in senior academic leadership within the discipline.

title: Distorted Perception of Facts as a Leadership Liability: A Comparative Case Study of Lee Iacocca and Donald Trump
summary: This paper examines a common factor in the leadership trajectories of Lee Iacocca andDonald Trump: a distorted perception of facts that privileges narrative coherence overempirical accuracy. Drawing on documentary evidence from corporate governance records,fact-checking archives, biographical accounts, and psychological research, the paperidentifies a shared mechanism in which selective factual presentation, reframing of failure as success, blame externalization, and resistance to institutional checks operate as a coherent operating system. The paper argues that while Iacocca’s distorted perception was eventuallyconstrained by the institutional checks of corporate governance and market accountability,Trump’s operates within a fragmented media and political ecosystem that allows thedistortion to persist longer. The comparative framework suggests that distorted perception is not merely a personal failing but a structurally contingent leadership strategy whose durability depends on the strength of the reality-testing institutions surrounding the leader.

title: Green Financial Literacy and ESG Awareness to Sustainable Investment Intention: The Mediating Role of Green Trust
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Green Financial Literacy and ESG Awareness on Sustainable Investment Intention and to examine the role of Green Trust as a mediating variable among young investors in Indonesia. The study employs a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design. Data were obtained through an online survey of 327 investors aged 18–40 years holding a Single Investor Identification (SID). Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Results indicate that Green Financial Literacy positively and significantly influences Green Trust (β = 0.348; p < 0.001), as does ESG Awareness on Green Trust (β = 0.326; p < 0.001). Green Trust emerges as the strongest direct predictor of Sustainable Investment Intention (β = 0.438; p < 0.001). Furthermore, Green Financial Literacy (β = 0.154; p = 0.004) and ESG Awareness (β = 0.142; p = 0.008) positively and significantly influence Sustainable Investment Intention directly. Green Trust also mediates the relationship between Green Financial Literacy and Sustainable Investment Intention (indirect effect = 0.152; p < 0.001) and between ESG Awareness and Sustainable Investment Intention (indirect effect = 0.143; p < 0.001). The model explains 41.2% of the variance in Green Trust and 52.7% of the variance in Sustainable Investment Intention. This study contributes to the literature by examining Green Financial Literacy as a sustainability-specific construct, identifying Green Trust as a mechanism connecting cognitive factors with sustainable investment intention, and providing empirical evidence from the context of young Indonesian investors. Findings suggest that knowledge and ESG awareness are not fully translated into investment intention without trust in the credibility of the sustainable financial ecosystem. These findings indicate that increasing sustainable investment requires a combination of strengthening green financial literacy and building trust. Financial institutions need to enhance education regarding sustainable financial products and ESG information transparency, while regulators need to strengthen ESG disclosure standardization and oversight of greenwashing practices. These efforts can strengthen investor trust and support the growth of sustainable investment in Indonesia.

title: Comparing the resilience of multi-hub supply chain networks under port disruption scenarios: a case study of Singapore, Port Klang and Tanjung Pelepas
summary: Major transshipment hubs improve operational efficiency through cargo concentration but can transmit local disruptions across maritime supply chains. Existing research recognises network redundancy yet insufficiently distinguishes the presence of backup hubs from their deployable capacity. Using Singapore, Port Klang, and Tanjung Pelepas as a regional case, this study compares four network configurations across five disruption scenarios. A linear programming model allocates cargo flows while evaluating demand fulfillment and relative total cost; sensitivity analysis examines backup capacity assumptions. The findings show that additional hubs do not automatically generate resilience. Service continuity depends on whether deployable backup capacity covers the demand shortfall created by disruption at the primary hub. Under a 75% capacity loss at the Port of Singapore, the multi-hub configuration achieved a demand fulfillment rate of 57.76%, which was 32.76 percentage points higher than that of the single-hub configuration, while recording a lower relative total cost of 445.78 compared with 750.00. Dual-hub configurations also performed differently because alternative ports varied in usable capacity and rerouting costs. Overall, redundancy improved both service continuity and relative cost performance when the disruption losses it avoided exceeded the additional coordination and rerouting costs. This paper therefore offers a conditional theoretical interpretation for effective network redundancy and proposes the principle of capacity‑matched selective diversification, which can guide the design of regional transshipment networks.

title: Does Green Innovation Alleviate or Aggravate Financing Constraints? — Uncovering a Nonlinear Threshold Effect: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Green innovation has been a highly debated topic, which is increasingly important for market entities, especially firms and policy makers. Nevertheless, the advancement of green innovation is constrained by its inherent characteristics: high upfront investment, long payback periods, and substantial risks. This paper selects Chinese A-share listed companies from 2015 to 2024 as the initial research sample, and elaborates on the nonlinear relationship between corporate green innovation (measured by green patent counts) and financing constraints represented by the SA index, filling the research gap in existing relevant studies and providing solid empirical evidence to support the formulation, implementation and optimization of green innovation supporting policies. Using panel data, fixed-effects models, and heterogeneity tests, this study examines the inverted U-shaped relationship between green innovation and financing constraints. The findings offer empirical clarification on how green innovation alleviates financing constraints, and carry meaningful implications for stimulating market vitality and advancing high-quality green transformation.

title: Dilemmas and Tripartite Optimization of Banks' Green Credit Development under Dual Carbon Target
summary: Against the background of China's dual-carbon goals, green credit has expanded rapidly in China, yet problems including green-washing, heterogeneous cost pressure among different banks and potential systemic financial risks remain prominent. Most existing tripartite evolutionary-game studies on green credit only focus on direct interactions among governments, banks and enterprises, ignoring climate-policy uncertainty and supply-chain ESG spillover effects. This paper extends the tripartite evolutionary-game framework by introducing climate-risk shock parameters and supply-chain ESG-collaboration mechanisms. Numerical simulation under three groups of parameter settings identifies multiple equilibrium outcomes: lose-lose equilibrium, gradual win-win equilibrium and rapid win-win equilibrium. Drawing on EU Taxonomy and CSRD as reference, this paper conducts neutral cross-national parameter comparison and interprets how differences in disclosure requirements, penalty intensity and incentive magnitude change game convergence paths. Considering ownership heterogeneity among state-owned, joint-stock, urban and rural commercial banks, tiered risk-control, assessment and product-innovation schemes are proposed according to simulation outputs. The research shows that insufficient initial strict supervision may push the system toward the lose-lose state; appropriately raising incentives and penalties can accelerate tripartite win-win convergence. Institutional experience from the EU can provide references, but cannot be directly copied. Targeted differentiated governance for various types of banks helps to realize stable government-bank-enterprise win-win equilibrium.

title: A Study of AI-Driven Financial Inclusion and Sustainable Fintech Development in Dadar
summary: Abstract Financial inclusion has become a key part of economic development and is essential for providing easy and low-cost access to financial services to individuals and businesses. From machine learning to AI-powered predictive analytics, AI-driven tools like robo-advisory platforms, biometric authentication, and chatbots have improved financial institutions' access to previously unreached groups. The use of digital payment systems, mobile banking apps, and AI-powered financial platforms has helped raise awareness and participation in the formal financial system, particularly in urban areas like Dadar, Mumbai. The present study aims to explore the position of AI in financial inclusion for promoting sustainable advancement of FinTech in Dadar. This study aims to shed light on how AI technologies enable financial accessibility, overcome operational challenges, enhance customer engagement, and drive sustainable financial growth. Trends and developments in the financial sector are analyzed using secondary information from government reports, publications of Reserve Bank India, industry reports on FinTech, research articles and statistical databases. title: Authentic or strategic ESG? Motive attribution, consumer–company identification and purchase intention in retailing
summary: Against the backdrop of widespread greenwashing skepticism, consumers are increasingly scrutinizing corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) motives rather than simply accepting ESG disclosures at face value, creating a fundamental ethical dilemma in which ESG investment may fail to translate into market returns if corporate actions are attributed to strategic calculation rather than genuine values. Drawing on attribution theory and social identity theory, this study examines how Chinese retail consumers internalize ESG perceptions, through sincere versus strategic motive judgments, into consumer-company identification (CCI), and how this psychological process ultimately drives purchase intention, using a multi-study design in which Study 1 (N = 226) employed a cross-sectional survey of Chinese retail consumers to test the associative pathways and mediation effects among the key variables, while Study 2 (N = 156) employed a single-factor, two-level between-subjects experiment with structural equation modeling (SEM) and 5000-resample bootstrap estimation to examine the proposed direct and indirect effects. Three core findings emerge. First, corporate ESG performance exerts a robust positive effect on purchase intention even in skeptical environments. Second, CCI serves as the critical psychological bridge linking ESG performance to market response. Third, experimental causal evidence reveals that sincere motive attribution is the key trigger for activating CCI, with the indirect effect through identification accounting for 38.3% of the total effect, revealing a “dual-channel structure” in which a direct effect and an indirect, identification-mediated effect coexist. These findings offer actionable implications for ESG communication strategy in China's retail sector and provide a basis for future comparative research in other Asia-Pacific emerging markets.

title: Major Customer Network and Modern Slavery Incidents
summary: ABSTRACT This study explores the impact of major customer network structure on the risk of modern slavery incidents. By focusing on the downstream segment of the supply chain, the study aims to clarify how relational dynamics with major customers shape a supplier's exposure to labor‐related ethical violations. Using a panel data set of 1943 U.S. public firms from 2007 to 2022, the study examines the relationship between two customer network attributes, mutual dependence and customer interconnection, and modern slavery incidents. Modern slavery incidents are proxied by publicly reported labor‐related incidents that fall into categories classified as forms of modern slavery. The empirical results show that mutual dependence between suppliers and customers increases the likelihood of modern slavery incidents, whereas greater interconnection among customers reduces this risk. These findings reflect two underlying mechanisms: customers' dependence on suppliers can weaken their incentives to impose stringent sustainability requirements, while greater interconnection among customers facilitates information sharing and reputational pressures that strengthen monitoring. This study provides new evidence on how the structure of customer‐side supply chain networks shapes firms' exposure to severe labor abuses.

title: Strategic Alignment vs. Operational Reality: Analyzing Structural Friction Between International Corporate Governance Mandates and Performance Indicators (KPIs) in High-Velocity Global Industries
summary: Dominant theoretical models in corporate governance and management control systems assume that Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are linearly designed to maximize long-term economic value, optimize resource allocation, and foster rational organizational behavior. However, empirical evidence derived from managerial practice within large-scale corporations reveals a systematic and profound fracture between the strategic directives issued by global boards and the operational reality faced by local subsidiaries. This study explores and maps the structural pathologies and logical short-circuits generated by misaligned incentive frameworks that institutionalize a form of organizational schizophrenia, compelling management to navigate distorted ethical and operational trade-offs to satisfy formal numerical metrics.From a methodological standpoint, to ensure the highest standards of confidentiality, reputational protection, and absolute anonymity for all entities involved, the research adopts a qualitative approach anchored in the paradigms of Analytical Autoethnography and Aggregated Multi-Case Synthesis. The empirical dataset draws from the author’s direct participant observation and fieldwork, accumulated over a span of more than twenty-five years in managerial positions within multiple multinational corporations. Operational data and corporate occurrences have been entirely stripped of sectoral, chronological, and geographic coordinates, subsequently deconstructed and synthesized into four macro-archetypes of asynchronous corporate behavior: (1) Volume Hypertrophy at Negative Margins, (2) Dogmatic Compliance to Centralized Planning, (3) The Asymmetric Premium Positioning Illusion, and (4) Reverse Financial Engineering and Mix Coercion.In alignment with Goodhart’s Law, this study demonstrates how rigid quantification and the obsession with quarterly metrics drive boards to reward ritualistic efficiency while actively penalizing the logical and constructive dissent of rational managers. The paper bridges a critical gap in business ethics and general management literature, providing future chief executives and control committees with pragmatic guidelines to design flexible KPI architectures anchored to real-world market dynamics, thereby safeguarding the strategic, financial, and human integrity of the global enterprise.

title: Reconfiguring global value chains for low-carbon technologies and critical minerals: Evidence from solar photovoltaics, batteries, hydrogen and mineral supply chains
summary: The low-carbon transition is reorganizing global value chains (GVCs) for technologies and materials, yet existing evidence remains fragmented across individual sectors. This study conducts an integrated systematic–semantic review of solar photovoltaics, batteries, hydrogen and critical minerals. Based on 1934 Web of Science studies published during 2010–2025, it combines pruned exact linear time (PELT) change-point detection, Sentence-BERT semantic alignment, technology-specific qualitative coding and forecasting-oriented evidence synthesis. The results identify 2017 and 2021 as robust macro-breakpoints, marking a transition from the formation stage to accelerated expansion and then to a high-volume resilience-and-governance stage. Six thematic clusters structure the field: production, infrastructure and deployment; energy-system integration and transition; critical-material security and sourcing; life-cycle emissions and sustainability; modeling and economics; and supply networks. Technology-specific analysis identifies four reconfiguration mechanisms: mature-chain strategic diversification in solar PV, material-constrained circular scaling in batteries, coordinated chain formation in hydrogen and diversified upstream constraint governance in critical minerals. Semantic alignment is strongest with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7, SDG 9 and SDG 12, whereas alignment with SDG 13 and SDG 17 remains comparatively weaker. Overall, the energy transition should be understood not only as technological substitution but also as a differentiated and interdependent global value-chain transition.

title: The Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework: AI-Augmented Library Services for Inclusive Digital Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Innovation towards Viksit Bharat @2047
summary: Abstract India’s Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a knowledge-driven digital economy powered by artificial intelligence, inclusive entrepreneurship, FinTech, e-commerce and sustainable practices. Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions remain under-utilised as active intermediaries between knowledge resources and the competencies demanded by the future of work. This paper coins the Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework—an original, multi-layered LIS model that positions academic and public libraries as AI-enabled hubs for digital-commerce literacy, ethical information services and sustainable innovation. The study adopts a conceptual-constructive design that synthesises LIS theory, digital-economy literature, AI-ethics guidelines and national policy documents (NEP-2020, Digital India, Startup India). The KCB Framework comprises four interdependent layers: (1) Infrastructure and Multilingual Access, (2) AI Knowledge Processing, (3) User-Centric Commerce Services and (4) Ethical-Sustainable Governance. The framework is offered as a replicable, emulable blueprint that other institutions can adapt, pilot and scale, thereby leaving a durable mark on both scholarship and practice.

title: The impact of corporate governance on enhancing financial performance through risk management (An analytical study of the opinions of a sample of managers in some banks in the city of Sulaymaniyah / Kurdistan Region of Iraq)
summary: The digitization of human resource management has become a modern trend attracting increasing attention in contemporary organizations due to its active role in developing administrative practices and improving the efficiency of human resource utilization. The digitization of human resource management refers to the use of digital technologies and electronic systems to expedite procedures, reduce errors, and improve the quality of administrative services. Digital systems also help organize work and clearly distribute tasks, which positively impacts task performance and raises employee performance levels. Based on this, this research aims to investigate the role of the digitization of human resource management as an independent variable in improving job performance as a dependent variable, with its dimensions of: (task performance, contextual performance, and anti-productivity behaviors). Two main hypotheses were formulated, from which three sub-hypotheses branched out, to test the correlation and influence relationships between the research variables. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The study population consisted of human resources working in the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate, totaling (1001) respondents, while the study sample comprised (129) respondents selected using random sampling. The research data was collected by distributing 150 questionnaires to human resources personnel working at the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate. 129 questionnaires were returned and deemed valid for statistical analysis. The results showed a statistically significant positive relationship between the digitization of human resources management and job performance. Furthermore, the results indicated a significant impact of digitized human resources management on job performance across its three dimensions. Based on these findings, the research suggests the necessity of sustainably investing in and promoting digitized applications in human resources management at the Duhok Governorate Traffic Directorate to support improved job performance among its employees. The research also suggests conducting future studies addressing other relevant variables.

title: Beyond Digital Dependence: Accounting Information System Resilience and Contingency Strategies for System Disruption
summary: The digital transformation of accounting has fundamentally changed how organisations capture, process, store and communicate financial information. Accounting information systems (AIS), enterprise resource planning platforms and cloud-based accounting applications have enhanced transaction processing, information availability, integration and reporting. However, the increasing centrality of these technologies creates a less examined question: how can critical accounting activities continue when the primary information system becomes unavailable? This study develops a conceptual framework for accounting information system resilience by synthesising literature on accounting information systems, technology adoption, organisational resilience, business continuity, systems dependability and accounting practice, with particular attention to evidence from Nigeria and the broader international literature. The study adopts a qualitative conceptual research design based on a structured literature review and thematic synthesis. The analysis indicates that AIS dependence is multidimensional, extending beyond software to data accessibility, network connectivity, power and infrastructure, third-party platforms, and specialised human capabilities. Existing literature demonstrates the benefits of AIS adoption and flexibility for organisational performance and resilience, but comparatively less attention has been given to the continuity of accounting processes when the primary AIS itself is disrupted. The study therefore conceptualises resilience as the organisational capability to anticipate AIS disruption, maintain minimum viable accounting operations through appropriately designed alternative mechanisms, preserve information integrity, restore the primary environment and reconcile contingency records. On this basis, an Accounting Information System Resilience Framework is proposed, integrating preparedness, disruption assessment, contingency activation, continuity accounting, recovery and reconciliation, and post-incident learning. The study contributes to AIS scholarship by extending the discussion from adoption and system effectiveness under normal conditions toward accounting continuity under disruption. It further argues that resilience does not require abandoning digital accounting; rather, it requires a deliberately designed layer of alternative capability around the primary digital system.

title: Climate-Related Stress Testing and ESG Risk Management in European Banking Portfolios: Evidence on Physical and Transition Risk, Resilience, and Strategic Transformation
summary: Climate-related stress testing translates physical and transition hazards into banking losses, yet European exercises differ materially in horizon, balance-sheet assumptions, portfolio coverage, and purpose. This article asks what those exercises reveal about the resilience of European banking portfolios and how environmental, social, and governance risk management must develop. A structured comparative review of the twelve supplied supervisory publications and recent peer-reviewed research finds that aggregate systems generally absorb tested losses, but resilience is conditional. Disorderly transition produces concentrated impairment in carbon-intensive sectors, whereas unmitigated physical risk dominates over longer horizons through collateral damage, business interruption, and declining insurance. Reported losses are often lower bounds because market, liquidity, operational, litigation, and second-round channels remain incomplete. Banks should therefore integrate counterparty transition plans, geocoded collateral, climate-sensitive credit parameters, dynamic multi-hazard scenarios, and links to pricing, provisioning, capital planning, and portfolio strategy. Orderly transition is the least-cost route, provided that steering supports credible corporate adjustment rather than abrupt or socially regressive withdrawal.

title: The two faces of digitalization: dimension-specific panel evidence from post-2004 EU labor markets
summary: Purpose This article examines how different dimensions of digitalization are associated with unemployment in the post-2004 EU member states, focusing on the heterogeneous channels through which digital transformation influences labor market performance. Design/methodology/approach The analysis applies panel regression to annual data for the period 2016–2023, modeling unemployment as a function of the four dimensions of the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) alongside relevant macroeconomic and structural controls, with lagged specifications. Findings The findings indicate that digital public services are associated with lower unemployment, while digital technology integration is associated with higher unemployment with a time lag, reflecting short-term labor-market adjustment processes. Practical implications The results suggest that institutional digitalization can deliver labor market benefits. In contrast, firm-level digital adoption and upskilling require complementary policies to manage adjustment frictions and support labor reallocation. This underlines the importance of sequencing digital transformation policies to balance efficiency gains with labor market stability. Originality/value This paper provides novel econometric evidence on the differentiated and dynamic associations between digitalization and unemployment in post-2004 EU economies by distinguishing between contemporaneous and lagged impacts across digitalization dimensions.

title: Improving the methodology for conducting an internal audit of fixed assets of a machine-building enterprise
summary: In today’s economic conditions, one of the factors contributing to an organization’s sustainable development is improving the use of its assets. The fixed assets used by organizations serve as their most important economic resource, influencing the increase in capital productivity, the number of services provided, the reduction in their cost, and, most importantly, the growth of profits. Fixed assets (machinery, equipment, buildings, structures, etc.) form the basis of the production potential of machine-building enterprises. Their technical condition, level of automation, and degree of wear and tear directly determine the volume of output, quality, and cost. Modernization and renewal of fixed assets are key factors in increasing production efficiency. Given the complexity and variability of the regulatory framework, as well as the large range of items and the geographical dispersion of fixed assets within a single enterprise, there is a need to organize an internal audit in order to comply with legislation in the field of accounting, monitor fixed assets, and improve the efficiency of their use. Based on a comparative analysis of economic literature and an assessment of these regulatory documents, the article systematizes existing approaches to the interpretation of the concepts of «internal audit» and «fixed assets», identifies their key similarities and differences, provides a critical overview of existing methods of internal audit of fixed assets and suggests an author’s methodology that takes into account the specifics of the engineering industry. Particular attention is paid to contradictions in the criteria for recognition of fixed assets, including cost limits and purposes of use, which creates risks of distortion of financial statements. The authors propose refined definitions of the categories under study, synthesizing modern requirements of international standards and national regulations. The application of the developed approach makes it possible to unify the process of asset identification, minimize the subjectivity of assessments and improve the quality of internal audits and control over the fixed assets of a machine-building enterprise.

title: Analysis of Operational Planning and Supply Chain of Used Cooking Oil to Support the Export of Biofuel Raw Materials: A Case Study of PT Biofuel Unggul Lestari
summary: Utilizing Used Cooking Oil (UCO) as a biofuel feedstock offers significant potential for development within the renewable energy supply chain. However, the UCO business faces challenges regarding supply availability, quality consistency, operational efficiency, inventory control, and the need for product traceability. This study aims to analyze the operational planning and supply chain of PT Biofuel Unggul Lestari (PT BUL) in supporting UCO exports for biofuel production. A descriptive approach using a case study method based on PT BUL's business plan was employed. The analysis covered operational design, cost-focus strategy, supply chain management, inventory control, quality management, digital technology utilization, and projections for operational costs and investment. The analysis revealed that PT BUL designed a supply chain comprising collection partners, UCO pickup, processing and storage, export operations, and international buyers. A cost-focus strategy is implemented through partnerships with collectors, facility efficiency, logistics control, transparent payment systems, and the use of digital technology. Established quality standards include FFA ≤3%, moisture ≤0.5%, and impurities ≤0.1%, while the supply readiness target is set at a minimum of 70% of buyer requirements. The inventory system selectively utilizes FIFO and JIT methods, with maximum storage periods of 7 days for raw UCO, 14 days for pre-processed UCO, and 30 days for ready-to-ship UCO. Projections indicate that UCO volume will rise from 800 tons in the first year to 1,800 tons in the fifth year, while operational costs will increase from IDR 9.96 billion to IDR 22.18 billion. The initial investment requirement is IDR 3.04 billion. These results demonstrate that the integration of procurement, quality, inventory, logistics, and digitalization is crucial for supporting PT BUL's operational readiness for the export market.

title: Determinants of Generation Z's Digital Gold Investment Interest Through Non-Bank Fintech Applications
summary: Generation Z's participation in digital gold investment remains relatively low despite the rapid growth of digital gold investment services through non-bank fintech applications in Indonesia. This study analyzes internal factors (investment knowledge and risk perception) and external factors (gold price fluctuation and electronic word of mouth) determining generation Z's interest in digital gold investment through non-bank fintech applications. Unlike most previous gold studies focusing on digital gold through banking platforms, this study highlights non-bank fintech applications amid user complaints regarding price accuracy, withdrawal speed, and technical issues found on social media. This study employed a quantitative associative-causal approach with purposive sampling. Primary data were collected via an online questionnaire on google forms using a four-point likert scale, distributed to generation Z in Indonesia who actively use social media and non-bank fintech applications, yielding 230 responses analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that investment knowledge, gold price fluctuation, risk perception, and electronic word of mouth each have a positive and significant effect on investment interest. These findings strengthen behavioral finance theory and provide practical implications for non-bank fintech providers to strengthen investor education, price transparency, platform security, and positive electronic word of mouth. title: Green Finance, Stage of Economic Development, and Low-Carbon Transition: Evidence from Dynamic Panel and Threshold Regression Models Using Chinese Prefecture-Level-City Data
summary: Green finance is widely regarded as a key policy instrument for China’s carbon neutrality goals, yet identifying its effect on low-carbon transition requires addressing green finance’s high correlation with regional development, and its nonlinear features remain insufficiently tested at a fine geographic scale. Using a balanced panel of 325 Chinese prefecture-level cities (2010–2022), this paper applies a fixed-effects model, Difference GMM, and System GMM, validated via an expanded Monte Carlo simulation, and Hansen threshold regression using the level of economic development as the threshold variable. Green finance is significantly and positively associated with low-carbon transition (2.175 under fixed effects, 3.294 under Difference GMM, both p < 0.01), with significant dynamic persistence; its direct effect is concentrated in the deployment period but propagates forward through this persistence. Two threshold values are identified (CNY 78.40 billion and CNY 160.44 billion), with effect strength rising from 0.558 to 2.180 as development advances, though the lower threshold is sensitive to the trimming proportion used, and System GMM’s insignificant coefficient reflects genuine, unresolved estimation uncertainty. These findings indicate that the green finance–low-carbon transition association is a structural process shaped by development stage, offering an evidence-based, though not precisely fixed, quantitative basis for staged, differentiated policy design.
